note:
# P-D-2019-1900007-65267201 - what this paper's figures teach

## Which section gets which exhibit
The paper models the same building twice, and the figure plan follows the halves rather than
the subsections. The 2D half (§§1.3-3.8) is all cheap vector drawing: a factors sunburst to
open, a plan-view storey for the assumption, one transformation diagram, two graph drawings,
one discretised node field and one flowchart - a schematic for every method subsection, each
placed at the end of the subsection that introduces it. The 3D half (§§4.1-4.3) switches
medium: two heat-map grids, a perspective surface, and a software render. The switch is
visible in the caption word 'Pathfinder' and in the colour bars: field exhibits get bars,
schematics never do.

## When three dimensions are worth drawing
Only where the object is three-dimensional: the floor stack of Figure 3, the surface of
Figure 9, the render of Figure 15 - plus one decorative case, the extruded pie of Figure 7,
which its own twin Figure 8 prints flat. That pair is the cleanest available demonstration
that extrusion is decoration: nothing but the slice mix differs between the two figures.

## Table type against data size
The one measured table is the notation list: 2 columns, 20 rows, booktabs, no verticals, no
shading, and a blank unruled row doing the work of a sub-header. The three data tables the
paper prints are all live text (Tables 1, 3, 4) with 4 to 12 stub rows and 2 to 3 columns,
i.e. below the size where these authors bother to draw a grid at all. Rule of thumb from this
paper: two-column definition lists get rules, small numeric tables get typeset as prose.

## Caption template
`Figure n: <noun phrase>` - 3 to 15 words, one sentence, no verb, no unit, no condition, no
conclusion. The caption never explains the panels: Part(I)/Part(II) are printed on the art and
counted in the prose. Two captions in this paper are verbatim copies of another figure's or
another table's caption, including the misspelling 'Framewok'; a caption is therefore evidence
about intent, not proof of identity.

## Context connectives
- Bare imperative as its own sentence, most often after a colon-like setup: "just as the
  following figure illustrates. See Figure 7."
- Inline pointer where the exhibit is the subject of the paragraph: "The specific factors we
  consider are shown in Figure 1."
- Parenthetical pointer for a detail inside a bigger drawing: "(The four blue circle in
  Figure 5 respectively represent one of the four frequently-used exits.)"
- Read-back sentence that restates the trend and never the numbers: "We can clearly see that
  90% of the evacuees leave the building from Exit #1, making this exit extremely overloaded."
- Sensitivity read-back naming the panel ordinal: "The third part of Figure 10 shows that the
  time of evacuation is not that stable when ... is smaller than 0.5."

## What this paper hands the lane
- The cleanest before/after pair in the lane: two composites, same recipe, one extruded and one
  flat, proving the 3-D effect carries no information.
- A duplicate-caption case at the exhibit level (Figures 10/11) and at the table level
  (Tables 3/4), so the caption field must be able to say "this text belongs to another exhibit".
- A third instance of the live-text table deficit, and the first where the unmeasured tables are
  numeric results rather than notation.
- A code-appendix pattern: ten listing regions whose running headers the heading detector reads
  as sections - refusals, not exhibits.

## The layer's own defects
Running head is live text with the folio inside it ("Team # 1900007 Page 5 of 26"); the Table 2
text layer interleaves its two columns ("Symbol Table 2: Notation dis(i, j) Definition ..."),
which is why the caption appears in the middle of the grid's own text; Table 1's rows merge in
the text layer ("Ratio of Young and not Disabled Visitors 72.1% 21.1%"); and ligatures (fi, fl)
plus split sub/superscripts break naive substring quoting throughout.
rules: A paper that models ONE building at TWO fidelities splits its figure families by half, not by section: the 2D half is drawn in schematic and plan vocabulary (six flowchart-or-schematic, one map-or-plan-view, one scatter) while the 3D half switches to field vocabulary (two heatmap-or-contour, one surface-or-3D) plus one software render [geometry.family].

The single axis-bearing exhibit in the 2D half is the discretised node field, printed in metres on both axes, and it appears at exactly the moment the geometry becomes numerical (the coordinate of each node) - the other seven exhibits in that half have no axes at all [geometry.printed_numbers].

Panels are NEVER sub-labelled (a)/(b) or (I)-(IV) in the caption. Where the paper needs to address a panel it either prints roman numerals on the art itself (Figure 9's Part(I) and Part(II)) or counts ordinals in the prose ('the third part of Figure 10', 'the fourth part') [geometry.panel_count].
Caption side is class-driven and has no exception in this paper: all fifteen figure captions print BELOW their art and the single measured table prints its caption ABOVE the grid [caption.position].

Both numberings carry a colon and a space this time - 'Figure 1:', 'Table 2: Notation' - the mirror of the previous paper's colonless 'Figure.1'. The number format is a house style, not a constant of the corpus, so it has to be read off the page every time [caption.numbering].

Sixteen captions, three to fifteen words, every one of them a single sentence and a noun phrase, with zero units, zero variable definitions, zero conditions and zero conclusions - caption economy is total, and the only information a caption adds is what the marks ARE [caption.words].

Two exhibits carry the SAME caption verbatim: Figures 10 and 11 are both 'The Framewok of the 3D Cellular Automata Model(3D-CAM)', misspelling and missing space included, although Figure 10 is the sensitivity grid and Figure 11 is the framework flowchart. The caption was copied with the template and never re-read; the figure number is the only thing that distinguishes them [caption.verbatim].

The same copying shows up in the tables: Tables 3 and 4 are both captioned 'Some Data we Use in the Basic Searching Model' although one lists plug-in values and the other lists results, and Figure 2's caption carries a stray trailing '2.' left over from an edit. Treat caption text as evidence about the author's process, not as a guarantee about the exhibit [caption.verbatim].

Colour bars appear only on field exhibits and never on the surface plot that most needs one: three of fifteen exhibits carry a bar (Figures 13, 14, 15, all Pathfinder density or time fields), while Figure 9's two jet-coloured surfaces are printed with no bar at all, so height can be compared between panels but never to a value [geometry.colorbar].

Legend placement is driven by whether the exhibit distinguishes SERIES: twelve of fifteen carry no key at all; the two composites key their pie slices outside-right (Figures 7, 8) and the four-panel sensitivity grid keys each of its three line panels separately inside the panel, so one key per frame rather than one key per figure [geometry.legend].

Three dimensions are drawn only where the object is three-dimensional and never as decoration of a flat quantity: the isometric floor stack of Figure 3, the extruded pie of Figure 7 (whose flat twin Figure 8 drops the extrusion because the slice mix is the point), and the perspective surface of Figure 9 [geometry.three_d].

The layout pass's heading weld mislabels two regions and both have to be corrected by the printed-heading rule: Figure 9 sits at the top of p15 above the 3.6 heading, so it belongs to 3.5, but the caption line welds it to 3.7; Figure 12 sits at the top of p18 inside 4.1, but is welded to 4.2 [place.section_path].

Exhibits are placed where the reading stops, not where the section starts: the factors sunburst opens 1.3 before any model exists, the simplified storey IS assumption 2.1, and each method subsection ends on its own schematic. Six of sixteen exhibits sit in the top third of their page, five in the middle and five at the bottom - placement tracks the remaining room, and the art is dropped at the page top whenever a new section follows [place.page_zone].

Citation is dominated by the bare imperative: twelve of sixteen exhibits are introduced by 'See Figure n.' printed as its own sentence, often a page before or after the art. Only two use an inline pointer ('are shown in Figure 1', 'The results are shown in Figure 8'), one is parenthetical ('The four blue circle in Figure 5 ...'), and one is a comparison ('like Figure 12') [mention.lead_pattern].

Four exhibits are named ONE PAGE BEFORE they print and exactly one is named one page AFTER: Figure 11 prints at the foot of p17 and is only named on p18 ('The framework of the 3D-CAM Model is illustrated in Figure 11'), the paper's only negative lead. Forward pointers are safe here because the art is parked at the page top and the pointing sentence sits in the text that continues past it [mention.lead_pages].

Read-backs exist only where the exhibit shows a sweep or a before/after: six of sixteen get one, and the sweeps get three (Figure 10 is read back once per varied input, in the order the panels were drawn). Single schematics get none - the paper never reads back a picture that only defines a construction [mention.read_sentences].

Sizes run 0.063 to 0.281 of the page and rank nothing: the largest is the notation table (0.281) and the smallest is the definitional triangular-cell schematic (0.063), while the figures that carry the conclusions - the before/after pair and the sensitivity grid - sit in the middle of the range [place.area_frac].

Table 2 is booktabs with three rules only, but it is split by an unruled BLANK ROW between the geometry symbols and the exit/time/mesh symbols, with no sub-header to announce the split, and one definition wraps onto a second line inside its cell - a two-column table that carries a hierarchy the rules do not draw [table.rule_style].

Three of the paper's four tables are live text with no measured region (Tables 1, 3 and 4 on pages 6 and 13), so the region count and the exhibit count differ by three and the difference is declared. This is the third paper in the lane with this deficit - after #147 and #174 - and the first where the hidden tables are DATA tables rather than notation tables [caption.verbatim].

The ten appendix regions on pp22-28 are MATLAB listings, refused as not-an-exhibit: no caption, no number, and a running header inside each listing that the heading detector reads as a section head ('4 C=X;', '24 D( i , j ) = 0 ;', '5 X=[X ; emerg ] ;') [place.section_kind].

Ten of the thirteen figure captions are still under twelve words and none exceeds fifteen, so the caption template is 'Figure n: <noun phrase naming the exhibited quantity>' with the condition carried by the prose and never by the caption - the shape a reusable caption template should imitate [caption.verbatim].

mention.lead_sentence: The primary notations in our paper are listed in Table 2.

tables.note: The notation list: two columns, twenty definition rows, three rules only (above the header, under the header, under the last row), no verticals, no box, no shading, no merged cells. Two structural oddities: an unruled BLANK ROW divides the geometry/space symbols from the exit/time/mesh symbols without any sub-header to say so, and the alpha definition wraps to a second line inside the cell ('(an independent variable reflecting the attribute of exit s)'). No numeric cells at all, so nothing to align. The only exhibit in the paper whose caption prints ABOVE its grid.
